result.title: PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes
result.summary: Large language models are increasingly used as judges to reduce reliance on costly human evaluation, yet their scores can systematically disagree with human judgments. We ask whether responses to an explicitly imposed evaluative bias can help correct a judge's implicit scoring biases. We introduce PRISM (Probe-based Residual Inference of Scoring Misalignment), which holds the evaluated content fixed and measures score changes when attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized. A local sensitivity model motivates representing these responses as a surrogate Jacobian. Ridge regression on human labels learns a correction to the baseline score. The resulting scoring protocol is rubric-free: it uses overall scores without requesting criterion-level ratings. In the main Jev and Sol comparisons on SummEval summarization and HANNA story evaluation, PRISM and its learned-baseline variant significantly improve agreement with human rankings over uncalibrated scores while remaining competitive with rubric-based methods. A controlled SummEval comparison yields similar agreement for rubric-derived quality probes and style probes, supporting calibration without reproducing rubric criteria. The learned coefficients reveal shared and opposing correction directions across judges.

AI.brief_summary: PRISM 在固定被评内容的前提下，通过强调或弱化属性构造反事实探针，测量黑箱评审分数的变化，将其视为替代雅可比并以岭回归学习对基线分数的校正，从而无需 rubric 即提升与人类排名的一致性，在 SummEval、HANNA 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反事实探针＋回归校正」的敏感性度量思路，可能可供核查 LVR 评估中评审分数是否对视觉证据与推理轨迹属性的强调做出合理响应，即把判分偏差与状态敏感性分离，具体对应关系仍需阅读原文判断。
